title: Add MFA to the VPN with Duo
domain: Secure Network Access, Visibility, and Enforcement
blurb: Put the Duo Authentication Proxy between the ASA and Active Directory so VPN logins need a second factor.
purpose: A stolen password is enough to log in to a VPN that only asks for a password. This lab adds Duo multi-factor authentication to remote access VPN with a RADIUS proxy. It covers MFA and how it plugs into existing AAA.
scenario: Remote access VPN users log in with only their AD password, and one of them was phished last month. Add **Duo multi-factor authentication**: the ASA sends RADIUS to a **Duo Authentication Proxy** at **10.10.99.50**, which checks the password against AD and then sends a Duo Push.
topology:
Secure Client ── ASA ── RADIUS ── Duo Auth Proxy 10.10.99.50 ── AD (primary)
                                              └── Duo cloud (push to phone)
objectives: Put the Duo login flow in order
Configure the proxy and the ASA AAA server group

steps.title: Factors
steps.learn: MFA combines different **kinds** of factor: something you **know**, something you **have**, and something you **are**. Two passwords are still a single factor.
steps.task: Match each item to its factor type.

fields.label: Duo Push to the user's phone

steps.title: The login flow
steps.task: Put the steps of a Duo-protected VPN login in order.
steps.question: Order from first to last.
items: The user enters a username and password in Secure Client
The ASA sends a RADIUS Access-Request to the Duo Authentication Proxy
The proxy checks the password against Active Directory
The proxy asks the Duo cloud for a second factor, and Duo pushes to the phone
The user approves, and the proxy returns Access-Accept to the ASA

steps.title: Configure the proxy
steps.learn: The proxy's **authproxy.cfg** has a primary authentication section (`[ad_client]`) and a RADIUS server section (`[radius_server_auto]`), which holds the Duo application keys and the ASA as a RADIUS client.
steps.task: Fill in the [radius_server_auto] section: the ASA at **10.10.99.1** with secret **DuoRadius1**, primary client **ad_client**, and **safe** fail mode.

steps.title: Point the ASA at the proxy
steps.learn: Duo Push waits for the user, so raise the RADIUS **timeout** to 60 seconds, or the ASA gives up before the user can approve.
steps.task: Create RADIUS server group **DUO**. Add host **10.10.99.50** on the **inside** interface with key **DuoRadius1** and timeout **60**. Then set tunnel group **RA-VPN** to authenticate with server group **DUO**.
steps.hint: `aaa-server DUO protocol radius`, `aaa-server DUO (inside) host 10.10.99.50`, `key DuoRadius1`, `timeout 60`, then `tunnel-group RA-VPN general-attributes` and `authentication-server-group DUO`.

commands.explain: Creates the AAA server group DUO using RADIUS.
Adds the Duo Authentication Proxy, reached through the inside interface.
Sets the RADIUS shared secret. It must match the proxy.
Waits up to 60 seconds, so the user has time to approve the push.
Enters the VPN connection profile's general settings.

commands.note: VPN logins now need the AD password and a Duo approval.
commands.explain: Sends VPN logins to the DUO group, which checks the password and then the second factor.

steps.title: Safe or secure fail mode
steps.question: The proxy can't reach the Duo cloud, and failmode is safe. What happens to a login with the right password?

options.text: It's allowed with the password alone, so an outage doesn't lock everyone out. With failmode secure, it would be denied.

options.why: That's failmode secure. Safe favors availability.

options.text: The ASA falls back to local accounts.
options.why: The proxy still answers RADIUS, so the ASA doesn't fall back.

summary: The three factor types, the Duo proxy flow from ASA to AD to the Duo cloud, the proxy's RADIUS server settings, the ASA AAA server group with a longer timeout, and the trade-off between safe and secure fail modes.
